## Introduction

This vignette describes an implementation of a Bayesian analysis without borrowing.

  
## Load the package

```{r setup, warning=F, message=F, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

library(BExTE)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Load the case study

The Belimumab case study ships with the package. `source_data()` reads the source (adult) study from its configuration.

```{r load_config}
config <- system.file("conf/case_studies/belimumab.yml", package = "BExTE")
src <- source_data(config = config)
src
```

The observed target (paediatric) study: 39 control and 53 treated patients, with 17 and 28 responders.

```{r}
tgt <- target_data(n_control = 39, n_treatment = 53,
                   responses_control = 17, responses_treatment = 28)
```

## Build the prior and fit the model

```{r}
prior <- separate_prior(src)
post <- posterior(prior, tgt)
post
summary(post)
```

`decision()` defines when the trial succeeds. Here it succeeds when the posterior probability of a benefit exceeds 0.975.

```{r}
success <- decision(critical_value = 0.975)
success(post)
```

## Plot the prior and the posterior

```{r, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
plot(post, xlim = c(-1.5, 2.5))
```

For advanced use, `post$model` is the underlying R6 model, of class `GaussianSeparate_RBesT`.
